subject: Post-demo pricing follow-up — expected monthly tokens, budget range & peak TPS
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lawson <emma@brightmesh.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jul 2025 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo pricing follow-up — expected monthly tokens, budget range & peak TPS

Hi Emma — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can put a concrete mutual action plan together.

Recap from call:
- Primary workload: customer support summarization + contextual search over product docs.
- Rough expected monthly consumption band: 20M — 80M tokens/month (currently prototyping at ~200k/day).
- Peak TPS (99th percentile burst): ~28 tps for short bursts during business hours; steady-state ~3–5 tps.
- Target economics you mentioned: aim for ~$25–$50 per 1M tokens depending on committed volume & SLA.

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm which of the two volume bands is closest to BrightMesh’s target for Q4? (20–40M or 40–80M)
2) Any procurement constraints on billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly invoice) or minimum term for a commitment?
3) I attached a pricing slab (redwood_pricing_slab_v2.xlsx) with 3 bands and unit $/1M candidates — please review and tell us which band aligns with your budget.

If that looks right, I’ll propose a short M.A.P. (mutual action plan) and lock a 30-min follow-up next week to finalize the commit and SLA.

Attachment: redwood_pricing_slab_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo pricing follow-up — expected monthly tokens, budget range & peak TPS

Vanessa — thanks for the summary and for the sheet. Quick clarifications from our side (per the call and internal sync):

- For Q4 we’re realistically targeting the 40–80M band if adoption continues as expected (conservative forecast: 45M/mo).
- Peak behavior: 25–30 tps bursts for the support channel during peak US hours, so your numbers align.
- Procurement: prefer monthly billing but happy to discuss a 6– or 12‑month term for better unit pricing.
- Budget: Dave (finance) gave a soft target of $30–$40 per 1M tokens if we can get predictable SLOs and a credit for throttling beyond SLA.

Also, procurement will want a short SOW and a standard data protection addendum. I’ve looped procurement in the cc.

—Emma

Date: Mon, 28 Jul 2025 09:13:22 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo pricing follow-up — expected monthly tokens, budget range & peak TPS

Vanessa — forwarding my quick take to include in the MAP before we send back to BrightMesh.

Key pricing notes (internal):
- If BrightMesh lands at ~45M/mo, we can propose Band B with a target of $36/1M as a starting point (6‑month commit) — preserves margin vs deeper 12‑month discounts.
- For peak TPS of 25–30, plan for a burst buffer option (reserve capacity) priced as an optional add-on — outline burst units as 200k extra tokens per minute for 15 minutes/day (estimate).
- SLA credit language: propose a small token credit (0.5% monthly) if 99th percentile exceeds agreed tps by >10% for two consecutive weeks.

Suggested next steps to include in MAP:
1) Confirm target band (BrightMesh) — Emma to confirm by EOD Wed.
2) We send a 1-page MAP + pricing slab for signature; procurement routes SOW concurrently.
3) Technical runbook and onboarding schedule (CS lead to own).

Attachment: brightmesh_mutual_action_plan_draft.pdf (draft MAP)

—Karthik

Emma — thanks for the fast turnaround and for looping procurement. Per Karthik’s notes above, here’s what I’ll do right away:

- Send a 1‑page MAP + updated pricing slab (Band B at $36/1M with a 6‑month commit) for you and procurement to review — I’ll attach both to HubSpot and shared Drive.
- Include optional burst buffer pricing as an add-on and the suggested SLA credit language.
- Schedule a 30-min alignment call for Thursday (Jul 31) at 11:00 AM PT to finalize band and invoicing cadence — does that work for procurement?

If procurement prefers a 12‑month downterm for a lower $/1M, we can present that as Band C in the doc.

Next steps (owner):
